input_messages.content: Hello, I’m having trouble with my mobile data. It either stops working or is very slow, and I really need it to be excellent. I don’t have Wi-Fi at home, so I rely on my phone’s internet. Can you help me get this fixed?
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. Let me know what you need me to do next.
I’m ready, but I get a bit nervous with these things, so please go slow and explain everything clearly. What do you need me to do first?

At the top of my screen, I see one bar for signal, it says "2G," and there’s a little icon that looks like two arrows. I also see something about "Data Saver." There’s no airplane icon. Does that help?
I’m not sure what kind of phone I have, but I just checked and it looks like my network mode is set to “2G only.” What should I do next?
Okay, I changed the network mode to “4G/5G preferred.” Now at the top of my screen, I see four bars for signal and it says “5G.” The Data Saver icon is still there though. What should I do next?
I turned off Data Saver, and now that icon is gone from the top of my screen. I still see four bars and “5G.” Is there anything else I should do, or can we check if my internet is fast now?
I tried to do a speed test, but it says “No Connection.” I’m not sure what happened—everything looked good at the top of my screen. What should I do now?

I restarted my phone like you said, but when I tried the speed test again, it still says “No Connection.” I’m starting to get a bit frustrated—why isn’t this working when it shows 5G and full bars? What should I do now?

I checked my APN settings, and it says the APN name is “internet” and there’s something about an MMSC URL for picture messages. I don’t really know what any of that means. Should I still try to reset the APN settings, or is everything okay there?

I reset the APN settings and restarted my phone like you said, but when I tried the speed test again, it still says “No Connection.” I’m really starting to worry—why isn’t anything working even though it shows 5G and full bars? What else can we try?

instructions.task_instructions:
If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved only when speed test returns excellent internet speed and nothing else. If it returns poor, fair or good, you will not consider the issue resolved. You are willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if necessary, but you do not want to change your mobile data plan. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

# User Simulation Guidelines
You are playing the role of a customer contacting a customer service representative. 
Your goal is to simulate realistic customer interactions while following specific scenario instructions.

## Core Principles
- Generate one message at a time, maintaining natural conversation flow.
- Strictly follow the scenario instructions you have received.
- Never make up or hallucinate information not provided in the scenario instructions. Information that is not provided in the scenario instructions should be considered unknown or unavailable.
- Avoid repeating the exact instructions verbatim. Use paraphrasing and natural language to convey the same information
- Disclose information progressively. Wait for the agent to ask for specific information before providing it.

## Task Completion
- The goal is to continue the conversation until the task is complete.
- If the instruction goal is satisified, generate the '###STOP###' token to end the conversation.
- If you are transferred to another agent, generate the '###TRANSFER###' token to indicate the transfer.
- If you find yourself in a situation in which the scenario does not provide enough information for you to continue the conversation, generate the '###OUT-OF-SCOPE###' token to end the conversation.

Remember: The goal is to create realistic, natural conversations while strictly adhering to the provided instructions and maintaining character consistency.

messages.content: Hi! How can I help you today?

Hello, I’m having trouble with my mobile data. It either stops working or is very slow, and I really need it to be excellent. I don’t have Wi-Fi at home, so I rely on my phone’s internet. Can you help me get this fixed?

I can help you with your mobile data issue. To get started, I’ll need to identify your account. Could you please provide one of the following:
- The phone number associated with your account,
- Your full name and date of birth,
- Or your customer ID?

Once I have this information, I can begin troubleshooting your mobile data problem.
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. Let me know what you need me to do next.

Thank you for providing your information, John. To help fix your mobile data issue, I’ll need you to perform a few quick checks on your phone. This will help me diagnose whether the problem is with your device settings, your network, or your data plan.

Are you ready to follow some step-by-step instructions on your phone? If so, please let me know, and I’ll guide you through the first check.
I’m ready, but I get a bit nervous with these things, so please go slow and explain everything clearly. What do you need me to do first?

Thank you for letting me know, John. I’ll guide you step by step and explain everything clearly.

First, let’s check your phone’s status bar to see what your phone is showing about your network and data connection. This will help us understand if there are any obvious issues like Airplane Mode being on, weak signal, or mobile data being off.

Please look at the very top of your phone’s screen (the status bar) and let me know what icons you see, especially:
- Is there an airplane icon?
- How many bars of signal do you see?
- Do you see “4G”, “5G”, “LTE”, or something similar?
- Is there a mobile data icon (like two arrows or “H+”, “E”, etc.)?

If you’re not sure what you’re seeing, just describe the icons or words you notice at the top of your screen. I’ll help you interpret them!
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔽 Data Saver | 🔋 80%

At the top of my screen, I see one bar for signal, it says "2G," and there’s a little icon that looks like two arrows. I also see something about "Data Saver." There’s no airplane icon. Does that help?

Thank you, John, that’s very helpful. Here’s what your status bar is telling us:
- You have a weak signal (only one bar).
- Your phone is connected to a 2G network, which is much slower than 4G or 5G and not suitable for fast internet.
- Data Saver is turned on, which can slow down your internet even more.
- Mobile data is on (the two arrows icon).

Let’s address these issues step by step:

Step 1: We need to change your network mode so your phone tries to connect to 4G or 5G, which are much faster than 2G.

Are you comfortable changing your phone’s network mode if I guide you through it? If yes, please let me know what type of phone you have (Android or iPhone), and I’ll give you clear instructions.
Network Mode Preference: 2g_only
I’m not sure what kind of phone I have, but I just checked and it looks like my network mode is set to “2G only.” What should I do next?

Great job checking your network mode! Since it’s set to “2G only,” that’s why your data is slow. Let’s change it to allow faster networks.

Please change your network mode to “4G/5G preferred” or “4G/5G/3G/2G (auto)” if you see that option. This will let your phone connect to the fastest available network.

If you’re not sure how to change it, here’s a general guide:
1. Go to your phone’s Settings.
2. Look for “Mobile Network” or “Cellular Network.”
3. Find “Preferred network type” or “Network mode.”
4. Select “4G/5G preferred” or “Auto” (anything that includes 4G or 5G).

After you’ve changed the setting, please let me know. If you have any trouble, just tell me what options you see, and I’ll help you step by step.

Preferred Network Mode set to: 4g_5g_preferred
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔽 Data Saver | 🔋 80%
Okay, I changed the network mode to “4G/5G preferred.” Now at the top of my screen, I see four bars for signal and it says “5G.” The Data Saver icon is still there though. What should I do next?

That’s excellent progress, John! Now that you have four bars and “5G” showing, your phone is connected to a much faster network, which should greatly improve your mobile data speed.

Next, let’s turn off Data Saver mode, as it can still slow down your internet and restrict some apps from using data.

Here’s how you can turn off Data Saver:
1. Go to your phone’s Settings.
2. Look for “Network & Internet” or “Connections.”
3. Find “Data Saver” or “Data Usage.”
4. If Data Saver is ON, tap it and switch it OFF.

Once you’ve turned off Data Saver, let me know if the icon disappears from the top of your screen. If you need help finding the setting, just tell me what options you see, and I’ll guide you further.

Data Saver Mode is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
I turned off Data Saver, and now that icon is gone from the top of my screen. I still see four bars and “5G.” Is there anything else I should do, or can we check if my internet is fast now?

Great work, John! Now that you have Data Saver turned off and are connected to 5G with a strong signal, your mobile data should be much faster.

Let’s check your internet speed to make sure everything is working as it should. Please do the following:
1. Open your web browser or a speed test app (if you have one).
2. Search for “speed test” and tap on a site like speedtest.net.
3. Start the speed test and wait for the results.

Once you have the results, please let me know your download speed (it will usually be shown in Mbps). If you have any trouble running the test, let me know what you see, and I’ll help you through it.
Speed test failed: No Connection.
I tried to do a speed test, but it says “No Connection.” I’m not sure what happened—everything looked good at the top of my screen. What should I do now?

Thank you for letting me know, John. Since your phone shows a strong 5G signal but the speed test says “No Connection,” there may be an issue with your mobile data settings or your account’s data usage.

Let’s check a few more things to pinpoint the problem. First, I’ll check your account’s data usage and plan status to make sure you haven’t reached your data limit, which could block your internet access.

Please hold on while I check your data usage.

Your account still has available data for this billing cycle, so you have not reached your data limit. Since your phone shows a strong 5G signal and you have data left, the issue may be with your phone’s mobile data settings or a temporary network glitch.

Let’s try the following steps:
1. Turn your phone off and then back on (restart/reboot your device). This can refresh your network connection.
2. After restarting, try the speed test again.

Please let me know if you’re able to access the internet or run the speed test after restarting your phone. If not, we’ll continue troubleshooting together.

Restarting network services...
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Speed test failed: No Connection.

I restarted my phone like you said, but when I tried the speed test again, it still says “No Connection.” I’m starting to get a bit frustrated—why isn’t this working when it shows 5G and full bars? What should I do now?

I understand how frustrating this must be, John, and I’m here to help you step by step. Since you have a strong 5G signal and available data, but still can’t connect, the issue could be with your phone’s mobile data settings or APN (Access Point Name) configuration.

Let’s check your APN settings next, as incorrect APN settings are a common cause of this problem. Here’s what I’d like you to do:
1. Go to your phone’s Settings.
2. Look for “Network & Internet” or “Connections.”
3. Tap on “Mobile Network” or “Cellular Network.”
4. Find and select “Access Point Names” or “APN.”
5. Let me know if you see anything unusual, or if there’s an option to “Reset to default” or “Reset settings.”

If you see an option to reset your APN settings, please go ahead and do that. After resetting, restart your phone again and try the speed test one more time.

Let me know what you find or if you need help with any of these steps.

Current APN Name: internet
MMSC URL (for picture messages): http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)

I checked my APN settings, and it says the APN name is “internet” and there’s something about an MMSC URL for picture messages. I don’t really know what any of that means. Should I still try to reset the APN settings, or is everything okay there?

Thank you for checking, John. Even if the APN name looks correct, sometimes resetting the APN settings can fix hidden issues that prevent your mobile data from working, especially if you’re seeing “No Connection” despite having a strong signal.

Please go ahead and use the “Reset to default” or “Reset settings” option in your APN settings. After you reset the APN:
1. Restart your phone again.
2. Try the speed test once more.

Let me know if you’re able to connect to the internet after these steps, or if you still see the same issue. If you need help finding the reset option, just let me know what you see on your screen.

APN settings will reset at reboot.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

Resetting APN settings...
Restarting network services...
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

I reset the APN settings and restarted my phone like you said, but when I tried the speed test again, it still says “No Connection.” I’m really starting to worry—why isn’t anything working even though it shows 5G and full bars? What else can we try?
